title: Is the banana really one of the best sources of potassium?

seo.title: Is banana one of the best potassium sources?
seo.meta_description: Bananas provide potassium, but potatoes, beans, lentils and avocado can provide substantially more in a normal serving.
seo.search_intent: Put the banana's reputation as a potassium source into nutritional context.

excerpt: Bananas are a good source of potassium, but they are not uniquely high. A medium banana provides about 420 mg; a medium baked potato can exceed 600 mg, and a cup of cooked beans or lentils can approach or exceed 700 mg.
content_html:
The banana is to potassium what the orange is to vitamin C: a useful food whose reputation has grown larger than its actual position in the nutrient ranking.

Real servings make the comparison clearer.

FoodServingPotassium
Banana1 medium~420 mg
Baked potato1 medium~600–900 mg
Cooked lentils1 cup~730 mg
Cooked beans1 cup~700–900 mg
Avocado1 medium edible portion / ~150 g~730 mg

A potato or cup of legumes can therefore provide roughly twice the potassium of a medium banana.

Why bananas became the potassium icon

They are portable, inexpensive and require no preparation. They also provide carbohydrate, which helped make them a familiar sports snack. Convenience, not record-setting potassium concentration, explains much of the reputation.

Cooking can change the number

Potassium is water-soluble. Boiling cut vegetables in plenty of water and discarding the water can lower potassium, while baking generally retains more. Preparation therefore matters when comparing values.

A serving changes the comparison

A medium banana provides roughly 420 mg of potassium. That is useful, but a medium baked potato can provide about 600–900 mg, around 200 g of cooked lentils roughly 700 mg, and a generous 150 g serving of avocado about 730 mg. Bananas therefore make more sense as a convenient source than as the food that contains the most potassium.

The comparison also shows why there is little value in chasing one “best” food. Legumes, potatoes, vegetables, fruit and dairy can all contribute potassium across the day while bringing fiber, protein and other micronutrients with them.

The practical conclusion

A banana is a perfectly useful potassium-containing fruit. It is simply one option among many, and potatoes, legumes, avocado and several vegetables can contribute more per normal serving.

faq.question: What has more potassium than a banana?
faq.answer: A medium baked potato, a cup of cooked lentils or beans, and a substantial serving of avocado can all provide more than a medium banana.

faq.question: Does cooking lower potassium?
faq.answer: Boiling can reduce potassium when some of the mineral moves into cooking water that is discarded.
